bounds: SentenceBoundary
Regulation Crowdfunding, often called Reg CF, is a U.S. securities exemption that lets eligible companies raise money from the public online.
SentenceBoundary
An offering must be conducted through an SEC-registered broker-dealer or funding portal.
SentenceBoundary
It is not simply a company posting a payment link and calling it an investment.
SentenceBoundary
The company files disclosures, usually on Form C, and investors review those documents through the intermediary.
SentenceBoundary
Non-accredited investors are subject to aggregate investment limits across Reg CF offerings during a rolling twelve-month period.
SentenceBoundary
The company may raise up to five million dollars under the exemption in a twelve-month period, subject to the rules.
SentenceBoundary
Securities bought in a Reg CF offering generally cannot be resold for one year, with limited exceptions.
SentenceBoundary
The SEC filing is not an endorsement of the company or a prediction that it will succeed.
SentenceBoundary
Read the offering carefully, verify the intermediary, and understand that startup losses and long holding periods are possible.
SentenceBoundary
These rules describe Reg CF, not every kind of startup fundraising.
